records.public_claim_text: At the sub-regional level, the legal framework for natural heritage is considered the least adequate in Eastern Europe (83%) and Western Europe reported the lowest rates of adequacy for cultural heritage (88%).
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: At the sub-regional level, the legal framework for natural heritage is considered the least adequate in Eastern Europe (83%) and Western Europe reported the lowest rates of adequacy for cultural heritage (88%).

records.public_claim_text: Legal frameworks were considered slightly less adequate for the conservation and protection of cultural heritage than natural heritage (76% and 82% respectively).
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Legal frameworks were considered slightly less adequate for the conservation and protection of cultural heritage than natural heritage (76% and 82% respectively).

records.public_claim_text: In addition, 47% of the States Parties have policies in this regard but experience some deficiencies in their implementation.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: In addition, 47% of the States Parties have policies in this regard but experience some deficiencies in their implementation.

records.public_claim_text: Sub-regional variations are observed: 22% of the States Parties in Southern Europe reported not to have specific policies in this regard and only 8% of the States Parties in Eastern Europe reported that they have policies that are implemented effectively.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Sub-regional variations are observed: 22% of the States Parties in Southern Europe reported not to have specific policies in this regard and only 8% of the States Parties in Eastern Europe reported that they have policies that are implemented effectively.

records.public_claim_text: The 2015 World Heritage Sustainable Development Policy is the most widely used policy across the Europe and North America region to set national policies or strategies for the protection of cultural and natural heritage (68% of the States Parties).
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: The 2015 World Heritage Sustainable Development Policy is the most widely used policy across the Europe and North America region to set national policies or strategies for the protection of cultural and natural heritage (68% of the States Parties).

records.public_claim_text: Over half (59% or 30 out of 51) of the States Parties reported to have adequate coordination and integration of the implementation of these multilateral agreements, programmes and World Heritage policies and strategies into national policies.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Over half (59% or 30 out of 51) of the States Parties reported to have adequate coordination and integration of the implementation of these multilateral agreements, programmes and World Heritage policies and strategies into national policies.

records.public_claim_text: It is interesting to note the high levels of involvement of communities and Indigenous Peoples in the development of inventories compared with the involvement of these same groups of actors in Tentative Lists processes, addressed in section 2.3 of this report.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: It is interesting to note the high levels of involvement of communities and Indigenous Peoples in the development of inventories compared with the involvement of these same groups of actors in Tentative Lists processes, addressed in section 2.3 of this report.

records.public_claim_text: 84% (43 of 51) States Parties use inventories/lists/registers for the identification of cultural sites for the Tentative List compared with 77% for natural sites and 67% for mixed sites.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: 84% (43 of 51) States Parties use inventories/lists/registers for the identification of cultural sites for the Tentative List compared with 77% for natural sites and 67% for mixed sites.

records.public_claim_text: Cooperation between the different levels of government and diverse segments of civil society is the same for cultural and natural heritage: 88% of the States Parties in Europe and North America reported effective cooperation overall.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Cooperation between the different levels of government and diverse segments of civil society is the same for cultural and natural heritage: 88% of the States Parties in Europe and North America reported effective cooperation overall.

records.public_claim_text: Financial status and human resources For most of the States Parties in Europe and North America the major sources of funding for running costs/maintenance are national governments (90% or 46 out of 51) or other levels of government, either at the provincial, state, or local levels (55% or 28).
